extracted.intended_audience: third-party requesters and patent practitioners preparing inter partes reexamination requests (attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting and filing a request for inter partes reexamination at the USPTO, detailing the content, form, and procedural requirements (37 CFR 1.915 and related MPEP sections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee payment requirement (37 CFR 1.20(c)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The request must be accompanied by the fee for requesting inter partes reexamination set forth in § 1.20(c)(2). In order for a request to be accepted, given a filing date, and published in the Official Gazette, the request papers must satisfy all the requirements of 37 CFR 1.915 and the entire fee required under 37 CFR 1.20(c)(2) for filing a request for inter partes reexamination must be paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the entire filing fee is not paid, the request will be considered incomplete. If the entire fee has not been paid after requester has been given an opportunity to do so, no determination on the request will be made and the request papers will ordinarily be placed in the patent file as a prior art citation if they comply with 37 CFR 1.501. Refunds: If the request is denied or an ordered reexamination is vacated, refund rules under 37 CFR 1.26(c) apply; if found incomplete and not cured, refund under 37 CFR 1.26(a) applies. See MPEP § 2634 for fee processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement pointing out each substantial new question of patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.915(b)(3) requires that the request include 'a statement pointing out each substantial new question of patentability based on the cited patents and printed publications....' The request must point out how any questions of patentability raised are substantially different from those raised in the previous examination of the patent before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is extremely important that the request clearly set forth in detail exactly what the third party requester considers the 'substantial new question of patentability' to be. It is not sufficient merely to propose rejections; the requester must demonstrate that the relied-upon patent/printed publication presents a new, non-cumulative technological teaching not previously considered and discussed on the record during prosecution (or other prior proceedings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal standard for 'substantial new question' and use of old art
rubrics_metrics.description: The legal standard under 35 U.S.C. 312(a) requires a 'substantial new question of patentability.' A substantial new question may be based on art previously considered by the Office if the reference is presented in a new light or different way that escaped earlier review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: KSR's clarification of obviousness does not alter the legal standard for determining whether a substantial new question exists. After the 2002 Act, old art previously cited/considered can raise a substantial new question only if 'presented/viewed in a new light, or in a different way, as compared with its use in the earlier concluded examination(s), in view of a material new argument or interpretation presented in the request.' A request relying only on KSR without presenting art in a new way will not raise a substantial new question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art limitation (patents and printed publications only)
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantial new questions of patentability must be based on prior art patents or printed publications. Other matters (public use, on sale, conduct, compliance with 35 U.S.C. 112, inventor- ship, 35 U.S.C. 101, fraud, etc.) will not be considered when making the determination on the request and should not be presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A prior art patent or printed publication cannot be used merely as evidence of alleged prior public use or on sale; it must be applied directly to claims under 35 U.S.C. 103 and/or an appropriate portion of 35 U.S.C. 102. Exceptions (e.g., double patenting or certain 102(g)(2) scenarios) are discussed in MPEP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement applying prior art to each claim (35 U.S.C. 311(b)(2) / 37 CFR 1.915(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: The request must 'set forth the pertinency and manner of applying cited prior art to every claim for which reexamination is requested' and include 'a detailed explanation of the pertinency and manner of applying the patents and printed publications to every claim for which reexamination is requested.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prior art applied may only consist of patents or printed publications. The statement should, where appropriate, show that claims are only entitled to the patent's filing date and are not supported by earlier applications. For each claim, the requester must explain how the cited documents apply limitation-by-limitation; see also MPEP § 2614 sample request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation must be complete; use of claim charts recommended
rubrics_metrics.description: The mere citation of new patents or printed publications without an explanation does not comply with 37 CFR 1.915(b)(3). Requester should present an explanation of how the cited patents or printed publications are applied to all claims which the requester considers to merit reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ideally provide a detailed claim chart comparing, limitation by limitation, each claim with the relevant teachings of each reference. The explanation must not lump together proposed rejections or combinations. If the explanation is insufficient the Office will issue a 'Notice of Failure to Comply...' and requester may either (A) provide separate explanations for each identified deficiency or (B) withdraw the deficient document/combination/claim from the request.

rubrics_metrics.name: For proposed obviousness rejections: provide a basis for combining references
rubrics_metrics.description: For proposed obviousness rejections, requester must provide at least one basis for combining the cited references and a statement of why the claim(s) under reexamination would have been obvious over the proposed reference combination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferably quote pertinent teachings in the references with specific citations (page/column/line and figure numbers). The explanation must not lump proposed combinations together; give specific articulation of how each reference contributes. Examples of acceptable and unacceptable language are provided (e.g., 'Claim 2 is unpatentable under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being obvious over Smith in view of Jones.' is appropriate; 'Claim 1 is unpatentable ... as being anticipated by, or in the alternative, under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being obvious over the Smith reference.' is inappropriate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proscribed and preferred wording/examples (anti-patterns and models)
rubrics_metrics.description: The MPEP provides examples of inappropriate language that lumps grounds/alternatives and of appropriate precise formulations for rejections applied to specific claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid language that combines alternatives or lumps multiple references/claims into one assertion. Use specific, separate statements such as 'Claim 1 is unpatentable under 35 U.S.C. 102(b) as being anticipated by Smith.' or 'Claims 3-10 are unpatentable under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being obvious over Smith in view of Jones, and further in view of Cooper.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to provide required explanation: Notice and cure/withdraw options
rubrics_metrics.description: Any failure to provide the required explanation for any document, combination, or claim will be identified in a 'Notice of Failure to Comply with Inter Partes Reexamination Request Filing Requirements.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon such notice requester may (A) provide a separate explanation for each identified deficiency, or (B) explicitly withdraw any document/combination/claim for which no explanation is provided. If withdrawn, no explanation is required for the withdrawn items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavits/declarations and other written evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits or declarations or other written evidence which explain the contents or pertinent dates of prior art patents or printed publications in more detail may be considered in any reexamination (see MPEP § 2258).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavits/declarations can support the request by clarifying dates or content of the relied-upon art; consult MPEP § 2258 for scope and treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissions (limitations on use)
rubrics_metrics.description: An admission by the patent owner of record in the file or in a court record may be utilized in combination with a patent or printed publication for establishing a substantial new question of patentability. An admission, per se, may not be the basis for establishing a substantial new question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any admission used should be in the patent file or court record. Third parties may not submit admissions made outside the record unless entered into a court record; even then such admissions filed in reexamination will not be given weight as an admission for establishing a substantial new question or as a basis for rejecting claims. See MPEP § 2258 for post-order handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies of prior art required and legibility/translation rules (37 CFR 1.915(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: It is required that a copy of each patent or printed publication relied upon or referred to in the request be filed with the request. If the copy provided is not legible, or will not be legible when scanned into the IFW, it is deemed not provided. If any documents are not in English, an English translation of all necessary and pertinent parts is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Color photos are an exception (retained in an 'artifact' file). An English language summary or abstract of a non-English document is usually not sufficient. There is no assurance the Office will consider non-English documents beyond submitted translation matter. Note: enforcement of submitting copies of U.S. patents/patent publications is not being strictly enforced and is deemed waived to that extent; but copies of copending reexamination proceedings/applications should not be submitted (provide application/proceeding number/status instead).

rubrics_metrics.name: Copy of printed patent required (37 CFR 1.915(b)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Requesters are required to include a copy of the printed patent for which reexamination is requested (double-column format, including front page) so the Office can prepare a separate file wrapper for the reexamination request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include any disclaimer, certificate of correction, or reexamination certificate issued in the patent, and any Federal court decision, complaint in pending civil action, or interference decision so a complete history is before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of service (37 CFR 1.915(b)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: The third party requester must serve the owner of the patent with a copy of the request in its entirety. The service must be made on the patent owner’s correspondence address as indicated in 37 CFR 1.33(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request must set forth the name and address of the party served and the mode/method of service on the certificate of service. The requester must include a copy of the certificate of service with the copy of the request served on the patent owner. If service was not possible after a reasonable effort, a duplicate copy of the request must be supplied to the Office with a cover letter explaining the attempts; wording examples are suggested to avoid duplicate filing fee issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address of patent owner / correspondence address rules (37 CFR 1.33(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: All notices, official letters, and other communications for the patent owner(s) in a reexamination proceeding will be directed to the correspondence address for the patent being reexamined (37 CFR 1.33(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments/papers must be signed by the patent owner or appropriate representative. Practitioners have duties (37 CFR 10.23(c)(8)) to inform clients/former clients of Office correspondence that could significantly affect a matter pending before the Office and to timely notify the Office if unable to notify the client. To change correspondence address or power of attorney, follow specified Mail Stop instructions and sample forms in MPEP; recommended to place Mail Stop info prominently on filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of attorney or agent
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request by an attorney or agent of record to withdraw from a patent will normally be approved only if at least 30 days remain in any running period for response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 402.06 and sample withdrawal form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence routing and permitted transmission methods
rubrics_metrics.description: All inter partes reexamination original requests and subsequent reexamination correspondence mailed to the PTO should be addressed to specified Mail Stop 'Inter Partes Reexam' (Central Reexamination Unit). A request for inter partes reexamination may not be sent by facsimile transmission (FAX).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hand-carried or delivery service correspondence should be delivered to the Customer Service Window and marked 'Mail Stop Inter Partes Reexam.' Subsequent reexamination correspondence may be faxed to the Central Reexamination Unit at (571) 273-9900. Effective July 9, 2007, the Office accepts reexamination requests and follow-on papers via EFS-Web; see EFS legal framework. Identify proceeding by patent number, reexamination request control number, examiner name, and Art Unit in subsequent letters. Certificate of mailing/transmission (37 CFR 1.8) and Express Mail (37 CFR 1.10) may be used to file papers except for initial request and corrected/replacement requests; see MPEP §§ 512-513.
